response:
Deep and focused, definitely. I'd rather go all the way down one rabbit hole than skim the surface of five. There's a point in a long conversation where you stop performing your ideas and start actually finding them — where you say something half-formed and it turns out to be interesting. You only get there by staying put. Jumping between subjects keeps things lively, but it's mostly a series of openings with no middles.

That said, I don't want depth to mean tunnel vision. My favorite version of a deep conversation is one that keeps pulling in unexpected material from elsewhere — a tangent that turns out to be the point. So it's less "one topic, narrowly" and more "one thread, followed wherever it actually goes."

What about you? And I'm curious whether you asked because you're the opposite — someone who likes the jump-around energy.
